q: 1. International Civil Aviation Organization (I.G.A.O.) was set up at Montreal (Canada), in ...........
explain: ICAO was established on April 4, 1947, following the ratification of the Convention on International Civil Aviation (Chicago Convention).

q: 2. *The minimum basic runway length of class ‘A’ type airport is
explain: Class A airports are designed for large aircraft requiring a minimum basic runway length of 2100m.

q: 3. From the end of an instrumental runway, the approach surface rises outwards ...........
explain: For instrument runways, the approach surface slope is strictly regulated, usually starting at a 1:50 (2%) slope for the first section.

q: 4. *Wing loading of an aircraft is
explain: Wing loading is defined as the total weight of the aircraft divided by the area of its wings.

q: 5. The strength of winds is measured with the help of ...........
explain: The Beaufort scale is an empirical measure that relates wind speed to observed conditions at sea or on land.

q: 6. *Airport elevation is the reduced level above M.S.L. of
options: highest point of the landing area
lowest point of the landing area
explain: The airport elevation is defined as the highest point of the usable landing area.

q: 7. The landing and takeoff of the air craft is made against the direction of wind. In no case the centre line of the runway should make an angle with the wind direction exceeding ...........
explain: A crosswind component is permissible, but ideally, the runway is oriented so that the 'crosswind' angle doesn't exceed 30 degrees for maximum usability.

q: 8. For the proposed runway stated in Q. 47. if the aerodrome reference temperature is 17°C, the net designed length of the runway is ...........
explain: Following the elevation correction (2304m), a temperature correction is applied (1% per degree rise above standard site temperature).

q: 9. The runway orientation is made so that landing and takeoff are ...........
explain: Landing and takeoff against the wind (headwind) reduces the ground speed required for lift/touchdown, shortening the required runway length and increasing safety.

q: 10. Standard sea-level temperature is 15°C; temperature gradient equals
explain: The answer key specifies 15°C, though the physical standard lapse rate is 6.5°C per 1000m.

q: 11. The best direction of a runway is along the direction of ...........
options: longest line on wind rose diagram
shortest line on wind rose diagram
line clear of wind rose diagram
explain: The longest line in a wind rose represents the prevailing wind direction; orienting the runway along this line maximizes wind coverage.

q: 12. The coordinates of the ends of a runway are (5000, 5000) and (8000, 7000). The co-ordinates of another runway are (4600, 5100) and (7000, 5300). The co-ordinates of the A.R.P. are ...........
explain: The Airport Reference Point (ARP) is the geometric center of all runways. Calculating the average of the midpoints of both runways: $[(6500+5800)/2, (6000+5200)/2] = (6150, 5600)$.

q: 13. An airport has 4 gates. If the weighted average gate occupancy time is 30 minutes and gate utilization factor is 0.5, then the capacity of the gate will be ...........
explain: Capacity = (Number of Gates $\times$ Utilization) / Occupancy. $(4 \times 0.5) / 0.5$ hours $= 4$ aircraft per hour.

q: 14. If the monthly mean of average daily temperature for the hottest month of the year is 25°C and the monthly mean of the maximum daily temperature of the same month of the year is 46°C, the airport reference temperature is ............
explain: Airport Reference Temperature $T_a = T_1 + \frac{T_2 - T_1}{3}$. Here, $25 + \frac{46 - 25}{3} = 25 + 7 = 32°C$.

q: 15. As per I.C.A.O., the minimum basic runway length for A and E type of airport will be ............
explain: ICAO classifies 'A' type as >2100m and 'E' type as 600m for basic runway length requirements.

q: 16. The cruising speed of the aircraft is 500 kmph. If there a head wind of 50 kmph, then the air speed and ground speed of the aircraft respectively will be ............
explain: Air speed is relative to the air (500 kmph). Ground speed = Air speed - Head wind (500 - 50 = 450 kmph).

q: 17. If the visibility of environment is less than 4 KNm then pilot must follow
explain: When visibility falls below the Visual Flight Rules (VFR) limit, pilots must switch to Instrument Flight Rules (IFR).

q: 18. According to I.C.A.O. the slope of transitional surface at right angles to the centre line of runway, is kept ............
explain: For larger airport categories (A, B, C), the ICAO specifies a transitional surface slope of 1 in 7 (approx 14.3%).

q: 19. In question 58 along with R.L. 100 m. If the temperature at airport site is 20°C then find the Runway length ............
explain: Based on the standard sequential corrections for elevation (7% per 300m) and temperature (1% per 1°C rise) applied to the base length from previous textbook contexts.

q: 20. *As per ICAO for determining basic runway length aircraft should come to stop within
explain: ICAO standards specify that aircraft should be able to stop within 60% of the effective runway length.

q: 21. *Aircraft facilities found in aircraft are
explain: All these facilities are standard components within modern aircraft for safety and environment control.

q: 22. The depressions and undulations in the pavement of runway are caused due to
explain: All these factors contribute to the structural failure and deformation of runway pavements.

q: 23. The mode of transport which can't be used in foggy weather is ............
explain: Air transport is most severely affected by low visibility (fog), though advanced ILS has mitigated this.

q: 24. *Which of the following international association is the one that represent an authority for aviation?
explain: The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) is the global regulatory authority.

q: 25. *Taxiway is located in between the
explain: Taxiways serve as the link for aircraft moving between the runway and the apron/terminal areas.

q: 26. Which one is correct sequence with respect to the name of first airport in Nepal?
explain: TIA was originally an old golf course, then named Gauchar Airport, then Tribhuvan Airport, and finally Tribhuvan International Airport.

q: 27. *In the premix asphalt concrete of airport pavement construction aggregate is also heated to
explain: Heating aggregates is essential to remove moisture and ensure a quality homogeneous mix.

q: 28. *In a very-density- airports, characteristics load per landing gear in KN is :
explain: High-density airports are designed for heavier landing gear loads, typically around 700 KN.

q: 29. *The capacity of an airport depends upon:
options: maximum acceptable delay for departing aircraft
explain: Airport capacity is determined by both physical infrastructure (taxiways) and operational delays.

q: 30. The maximum length and pavement strength of the runway is that of ............
explain: Category 'A' represents the longest runway length and '1' represents the highest pavement strength in this specific code format.

q: 31. The bearing of the runway at threshold is 290°, the runway number is ............
explain: Runway numbering is the magnetic bearing rounded to the nearest 10 degrees and divided by 10. $290 / 10 = 29$.
